Lead story is a fresh, distinct escalation: Monday night, a Saudi Arabian tanker and a South Korean tanker were struck within minutes of each other in the Strait of Hormuz; Tuesday around noon ET, US CENTCOM confirmed strikes on IRGC air-defense, radar, maritime and mine-laying targets along Iran's southern coast -- a second escalation beyond Sunday's already-reported Jordan/UAE strikes, not a restatement of it. This, combined with Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish stance pushing September hike odds to 57-72%, drove Tuesday's genuinely broad risk-off session (S&P -0.71%, VIX +9.52%, gold/silver -2.9%/-3.7%, oil +5.5-5.8%). 4 items below are dated 1-2 Sep (within 24-48h), satisfying the freshness bar. Gaps this run: no fresh SGX/HK-tech-specific catalyst found beyond what's already carried from last week; no fresh (last-10-day) rare-earth-specific news found (existing Lynas item, 26 Aug, remains latest) -- both flagged rather than padded with stale items re-dated.

items.headline: Fresh Hormuz tanker attacks draw US strikes on Iranian targets -- a second escalation beyond Sunday's Jordan/UAE exchange
items.summary: A Saudi Arabian tanker and a South Korean tanker were struck by unidentified projectiles within minutes of each other in the Strait of Hormuz Monday night. Around midday ET Tuesday, US CENTCOM confirmed strikes on IRGC air-defense, radar, maritime and mine-laying targets along Iran's southern coast (Bandar Abbas, Jask, Chabahar, Konarak, Minab, Sirik, Qeshm island); Trump called the strikes "large and powerful," citing the tanker mining and a missile attack on a US asset as justification. This is distinct from Sunday's already-reported Jordan/UAE strikes -- the second round of escalation in three days.
items.actionable: The direct cause of Tuesday's cross-asset moves (oil +5.5-5.8%, VIX +9.5%, gold/silver down on hawkish-Fed dynamics overwhelming the haven bid) -- a live, still-unresolved conflict that argues for treating the miners-sleeve drawdown as a rates story layered on a real but so-far-contained supply-risk premium, not a fundamental deterioration.

items.headline: Oil surges 5.5-5.8% on the Hormuz escalation; IEA projects a Q3 global supply deficit
items.summary: WTI closed +5.81% to $90.74 and Brent's proxy (BZ=F) +5.24% to $95.23 on Tuesday as the confirmed Iran strikes raised fears of a prolonged Strait of Hormuz disruption. The IEA cut its 2026 global oil supply forecast (~102 mb/d, -4.3 mb/d y/y) and now projects a Q3 deficit of roughly 1.8 mb/d -- a genuine structural tailwind for energy, not just a one-day headline spike.
items.actionable: A live, IEA-corroborated supply-risk premium supports the energy sleeve (USO/XLE) while the conflict persists; risk cuts both ways since prior rounds of this ~6-month conflict have each proven containable and partially reversed once tensions cooled.

items.headline: Gold/silver sell off on hawkish Fed repricing, not the war -- ISM and JOLTS add a two-sided labor picture
items.summary: GLD fell 2.86% and SLV 3.68% Tuesday as September Fed hike odds climbed to 57-72% (from ~35% pre-Jackson Hole) on Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish stance, with the 10-year yield near 4.81% (highest since Jan 2025) and dollar strength overwhelming the usual Hormuz-driven safe-haven bid. Underneath the hawkish narrative, labor data softened: ISM Manufacturing PMI came in at 54.6% (below the 55.2% consensus, down from 55.6% in July) and JOLTS job openings missed at 7.271M (vs ~7.33M consensus) with June revised down to 7.182M -- setting up a genuinely two-sided Friday NFP (cons 55K vs -23K prior).
items.actionable: Size any silver/miner-sleeve additions with the binary Sep 16 FOMC risk explicitly in mind -- today's ADP and Friday's NFP are the swing data that will confirm or reverse this hawkish repricing before it's locked in.

items.headline: RBNZ decision today; broad consensus for a 25bp hike to 2.75%
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand decides today (2 Sep, 10:00 SGT), with ANZ/ASB/BNZ/Westpac/Kiwibank consensus pointing to a 25bp hike to 2.75% -- a more unified vote than July's 3-3 split decision. ADP Non-Farm Employment (cons 47K, prior 44K) and the Bank of Canada decision (cons hold at 2.25%) also print today.
items.actionable: A genuinely heavy global central-bank week stacked on top of the already-live Fed hike coin-flip -- avoid reading any single day's print in isolation until Friday's NFP clarifies the broader rate path.

items.headline: Tencent unveils Hy4 AI model, claims narrow edge over Zhipu's GLM-5.3 and Moonshot's Kimi K3
items.summary: Tencent released and open-sourced Hy4 Preview, a 770-billion-parameter model with a 1-million-token context window, saying internal blind tests show it slightly beating rivals Z.ai and Moonshot on engineering and coding tasks. The company is integrating the model into its WorkBuddy tool and chatbot.
items.actionable: An incremental positive AI datapoint for a core holding, but China's tech majors remain structurally behind the global AI-hardware trade -- sentiment support for the existing 0700.HK position, not a standalone reason to add size.

items.headline: Xiaomi puts Xring O3 chip into mass production six days after third straight quarter of falling profit
items.summary: Xiaomi's self-designed Xring O3, built by TSMC on a 3nm process, entered mass production targeting a September foldable launch -- six days after Xiaomi reported Q2 profit down 42.6% on rising component costs. The company has now sunk over 20bn yuan (~US$3bn) into in-house chip development.
items.actionable: Vertical-integration capex during a profit slump is a legitimate long-term-moat story but a near-term margin drag -- treat as a reason to hold through the earnings weakness rather than a fresh bullish catalyst.

items.headline: SMIC's interim report beats -- revenue +23.1% YoY, net profit +39.8%; shares jumped 17.45% (A-share), 10.76% (HK)
items.summary: SMIC's 2026 interim report showed revenue up 23.1% YoY to RMB32.35bn and net profit up 39.8% to RMB2.3bn. The stock rallied on both listings on the print, pushing total market cap to roughly RMB578.2bn.
items.actionable: A strong fundamental beat for a direct portfolio holding -- the rally has largely already played out, so this is confirmation of the thesis rather than a fresh entry signal.

items.headline: JPMorgan downgrades OCBC to underweight, cuts DBS price target to S$63 from S$70
items.summary: JPMorgan downgraded OCBC to underweight (target cut to S$20.50) and lowered DBS's target to S$63 from S$70, while raising SGX's target -- citing asset-quality and geopolitical-risk concerns for the Singapore banking sector, a notable divergence from the sector's record 1H26 income prints.
items.actionable: A direct, negative read on two core portfolio holdings from a major house -- worth weighing against the banks' still-strong 1H26 income and margin data before adding to DBS/OCBC exposure.

items.headline: DBS Research reiterates Buy on Singtel, TP S$5.46, on Optus margin-expansion catalyst
items.summary: DBS maintains a Buy call on Singtel with an unchanged S$5.46 target, flagging management's internal target of OpCo EBIT reaching S$2.1-2.5bn by FY30, driven largely by Optus -- whose EBIT is expected to nearly double from S$488m (FY26) to roughly S$1.0bn by FY30.
items.actionable: A constructive multi-year read on Singtel's largest subsidiary supports the SGX sleeve's income thesis, independent of the Iran/Fed volatility.

items.headline: Senate schedules Sep 15 CLARITY Act cloture vote; Polymarket passage odds fall under 20% from a 58% high
items.summary: Majority Leader Thune has filed the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act for a Senate floor-debate cloture vote on 15 Sep 2026, after it passed Senate Banking Committee 15-9 in May. Polymarket's implied passage odds have fallen to under 20%, down sharply from a high of 58% earlier in the process.
items.actionable: A concrete, dated regulatory-risk catalyst landing the same month as the Fed decision -- a genuine near-term binary for the crypto sleeve worth watching alongside Friday's NFP.

items.headline: August set to be first month Ether ETF inflows overtake Bitcoin's; BTC ETFs end 9-day inflow streak
items.summary: US spot Ether ETFs pulled in $3.87bn in August versus roughly $750m in net Bitcoin ETF outflows for the month -- the first time this has happened. Bitcoin ETFs still logged $924.5m over 24-28 Aug before a $202m outflow on Friday ended a nine-day, $3.04bn inflow streak, while Ether ETFs extended their own inflow streak to 10 straight sessions.
items.actionable: A genuine rotation signal within crypto (ETH over BTC) rather than a broad risk-off move -- consistent with a rate-sensitive but not panicked market into the Sep FOMC/CLARITY Act double catalyst.

items.headline: Lynas misses FY26 profit despite record revenue as non-China rare-earth pricing surges; shares fell 5.9%
items.summary: Lynas Rare Earths, the largest rare-earth refiner outside China, reported record net income of A$222.4m for FY26 -- up from A$8m a year earlier but below the A$263.2m analyst consensus -- as costs climbed 37% amid a ramp-up of new Australian facilities. Revenue still jumped 76% to A$977.9m on record non-China pricing. China's rare-earth export curbs on MP Materials and other US/allied firms remain paused through 10 Nov 2026.
items.actionable: Confirms the non-China rare-earth pricing tailwind is real and accelerating, even as near-term cost/execution risk (Lynas's capex ramp) is the offsetting factor to underwrite before adding size ahead of the Nov 10 export-curb pause expiry. No fresher rare-earth-specific news found this run -- flagged as a genuine gap rather than padded.
